metaDescription: Four folding carts and wagons under $50 compared by weight, 60 to 220 lb ratings, fold size and wheels, with a clear take on who should pay more.
introParagraphs: Shopping carts at this ceiling are less about luxury and more about avoiding a bad purchase. The same four models appear across the cheapest tiers, so the useful question is which of them fits your errands: a quick walk to the market, a drive to a big store, a laundry trip, or a day out with chairs and a cooler.

We evaluated four distinct folding models: the DMI utility cart (7.5 lb, rated 90 lb), the Our Modern Space steel cart (60 lb rating), the ROSONG collapsible wagon (12 lb, 120L) and the Blomoba wagon (220 lb rating). Those are the only true models in this band, so we did not add filler. The two wagons are labeled as wagons because they are pulled, not pushed.
This guide ranks them by the errand they suit, and points out the exact specs the listings leave out, so you know what to check before you order.

products.badge: Best for Walk and Transit Errands
products.name: DMI Folding Utility Shopping Cart, 90 lb
products.description:
The DMI weighs 7.5 lb and is rated for 90 lb, which is the strongest weight to capacity ratio among the four. The listing says it folds flat, ships with a carrying case and is compact enough for a car or public transport. Its title also mentions laundry and stair use.

For someone who walks to the store or rides a bus, the carrying case is the practical detail. You can sling the folded cart over a shoulder while you board, then unfold it at the curb. The listing does not describe the wheel material or the handle height, so check both if you are tall or have rough pavements.

Against the Our Modern Space at 60 lb it adds 30 lb of rating for a similar footprint. Against the Blomoba at 220 lb it gives up a great deal of capacity, but you are not hauling a wagon through a bus door. If your weekly shop is mostly cans and bottles, this is the most sensible of the four.
products.bestFor: Walkers and bus riders carrying heavy groceries.
pros: Only 7.5 lb to carry when empty
cons: Wheel type is not in the listing
Not suited to bulky outing gear

products.name: Our Modern Space Folding Shopping Cart, 60 lb
products.description:
The Our Modern Space is a stainless steel folding cart with 360 degree swivel wheels and a 60 lb rating. The listing says it collapses to a little over 5.5 inch and suits groceries, laundry and packages. It is described as lightweight but gives no weight figure.

Its selling point is how thin it gets. Where the DMI folds flat in a case, this one tucks into a gap behind a door or beside a washing machine. The 60 lb rating is the lowest of the four, so it is a fit for one person or a couple buying fresh food, not for cases of water.

Against the ROSONG it is far narrower to store, and against the Blomoba it is a different category entirely. Buyers who live in a small apartment will value the fold more than the extra rating the DMI offers. A bigger 100 lb version of the same cart exists above this budget.
products.bestFor: Small homes where storage depth is the limit.
pros: Folds to a little over 5.5 inch
Easy to slot into tight gaps
cons: 60 lb is the lowest rating here

products.name: Blomoba Folding Wagon Cart, 220 lb
products.description:
The Blomoba is a folding wagon with a stated 220 lb capacity, the highest figure in this group. The listing describes a carbon steel frame, 300D Oxford fabric and 360 degree rotatable wheels, and says it holds tents, sleeping bags and folding chairs.

A wagon changes how you carry. Instead of a basket you push in an aisle, you get an open bed that you pull, which is better for a farmers market, a beach day or a tailgate. The listing gives no folded size or weight in the text, so check your trunk against the product page before buying.

Compared with the ROSONG, you get a printed capacity number but a lighter 300D fabric. Compared with the DMI, you gain volume and lose the ability to step onto a bus easily. It is the one to choose if the load is bulky more than it is heavy. If you need to see the fold before you commit, the product page images are the place to look.
cons: Folded size is not in the listing

products.name: ROSONG Collapsible Folding Wagon, 120L
products.description:
The ROSONG is a 12 lb collapsible wagon with 360 degree rotating front wheels and an extendable handle. The listing gives a folded size of 22 by 9.8 by 7.5 inch, a 1.2 mm steel frame and 600D Oxford fabric with wear resistant PU.

The heavier 600D fabric is the distinguishing detail against the Blomoba's 300D, and it suggests better resistance to scuffs from tools or gear. What the listing does not give is a weight rating, only a 120L volume, so it is hard to compare its strength directly.

In ownership, the stated folded size makes trunk planning easy, which the Blomoba does not allow. It is the better match for garden jobs and camping, and the weaker match for groceries, where the DMI or Our Modern Space wins on handling. For groceries it is the weakest of the four, because the wagon bed makes small items roll around and the handle is low. For a yard job it is easily the best fit among the cheapest models. It is also the one to check carefully for a weight rating before loading wet soil or stone.
products.bestFor: Garden and camping loads where fabric toughness counts.
cons: No weight rating in the listing
Heavier than the DMI at 12 lb

buyingCriteria.explanation: Walk up errands and store aisles reward a pushed cart with a tall handle, while outings reward a pulled wagon with a wide bed. The DMI and Our Modern Space are carts, and the Blomoba and ROSONG are wagons. Choosing the wrong format is the most common reason a cheap cart sits unused. Decide your top errand before you compare ratings. A useful test is to write down your last three trips and the heaviest item on each. If two of them involved a cooler, chairs or soil, you want a wagon. If they were all bags and bottles, you want a cart.

Only three of the four state a weight rating: 60 lb for the Our Modern Space, 90 lb for the DMI and 220 lb for the Blomoba. The ROSONG gives volume, 120L, which is a size and not a strength. Add 20 percent to your usual load to find your needed rating. If a listing gives no rating, check the product page before you rely on it. For example, a 25 lb shop with a 20 percent margin needs a 30 lb rating, which every rated pick here exceeds. A 70 lb shop needs about 85 lb, which points to the DMI and above.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Carry weight of the empty cart
buyingCriteria.explanation: The DMI is 7.5 lb and the ROSONG is 12 lb, and the others do not state a weight. Every pound matters when you carry the cart up steps or into a trunk. A cart that is heavy empty tends to stay home. For frequent lifting, the DMI is the clear choice. The ROSONG at 12 lb is 4.5 lb heavier than the DMI, which adds up over a year of lifting. The Our Modern Space and Blomoba listings do not state weight, so ask before you assume they are light.

Thin and flat are different problems. The Our Modern Space is a little over 5.5 inch deep, the DMI folds flat into a case, and the ROSONG folds to 22 x 9.8 x 7.5 inch. The Blomoba gives no folded size in its text. Measure a closet gap or trunk floor before you buy. The Our Modern Space is thin but still has height, so measure all three dimensions. A thin fold only helps if the gap is also tall enough for the cart.

Swivel wheels turn tightly in a store, and a tall handle prevents stooping, with 35 to 42 inch a common comfortable range. The listings here describe 360 degree wheels but not diameters. The ROSONG adds an extendable handle. If you have uneven pavements, look for the wheel size on the product page. A 360 degree wheel turns fully but can wander on slopes, so a handle you can grip firmly matters. The ROSONG's extendable handle lets taller users pull without bending. Handle height is not stated for the DMI or Our Modern Space.

Above this budget the options add removable liners, dual baskets and larger rear wheels, such as the SereneLife with a 110 lb rating. Under this cap those features are traded for simplicity. If you carry over 90 lb regularly, the step up is justified. Under this cap you accept basic fabric and unstated wheel sizes. Heavy daily use is where a higher tier repays the difference.

howWeEvaluated.title: Errand fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We sorted the four by the errand they suit: transit and stairs for the DMI, closets for the Our Modern Space, outings for the Blomoba and garden work for the ROSONG. A cart that suits no clear errand scored low. Format mattered as much as rating. For example, the DMI leads for stairs and transit, while the Blomoba leads for bulky outings. We asked whether a buyer could use each one weekly without frustration.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stated capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 60 lb, 90 lb and 220 lb ratings and flagged the ROSONG, which gives only 120L. We did not guess a rating for it. Ratings were treated as ceilings with a 20 percent margin. A rating of 60 lb versus 220 lb is the difference between a salad and a camping trip. We rewarded clarity over big numbers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: Empty weight and fold shape drove this score. The DMI at 7.5 lb led, followed by the ROSONG at 12 lb. We noted that two listings do not state weight. Folded dimensions mattered only where stated, so the ROSONG gained a point for giving them.

howWeEvaluated.title: Materials
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stainless steel on the Our Modern Space, carbon steel with 300D fabric on the Blomoba and 1.2 mm steel with 600D fabric on the ROSONG. Heavier fabric earned credit for scuff resistance. Fabric weave is a clue to abrasion resistance, not a measured result, so we treated it as a tie breaker.

howWeEvaluated.title: Price band logic
howWeEvaluated.description: With only four models available, we asked what each gives up against the others. Positioning is based on listing specs and buyer feedback, not hands on measurement. None of these four is a premium product, so the question was whether each does its one job cleanly.

howToChoose.intro: How you move the load changes how it feels.

cards.label: Pushed cart
cards.text: The DMI and Our Modern Space sit ahead of you on a tall handle, so you steer through aisles and keep the load in view. Pick these for groceries and laundry.

cards.label: Pulled wagon
cards.text: The Blomoba and ROSONG trail behind you on a low handle, and the open bed suits bulky gear. Pick these for outings where nobody is squeezing past in an aisle.

howToChoose.note: A wagon behind you is harder to watch in a crowd, and a pushed cart is harder to use on a long unpaved path. Pick the format before the brand.

faq.q: Which shopping cart under this budget should I buy?
faq.a: The DMI is the best all round pick for groceries because it weighs 7.5 lb and is rated for 90 lb. The Our Modern Space is better if storage depth is your limit. The Blomoba is better for outings. The DMI is the easiest to recommend because its two main numbers, 7.5 lb and 90 lb, are both stated.

faq.q: Why does the ROSONG not list a weight limit?
faq.a: The listing gives a 120L volume and a 1.2 mm steel frame but no rated load. That does not mean it is weak, but it means you cannot compare it with the Blomoba's 220 lb. Check the product page before loading it heavily. If you need a wagon with a rating and fold size both stated, you may have to look above this cap.

faq.q: Are these carts good for stairs?
faq.a: The DMI title mentions stair use but the listing does not describe a stair climbing wheel set. True stair climbers usually use a cluster of wheels and cost more. For a few steps, a light cart you can lift is the practical route. Lifting a 7.5 lb cart up a flight is easy, while loaded stair climbing is better handled by a dedicated wheel design.

faq.q: How much weight can a grocery cart really carry?
faq.a: Keep to about 80 percent of the rating. At 60 lb the Our Modern Space suits light shops, and the DMI at 90 lb suits heavier ones. Cans, bottles and pet food add weight fast. Distribute heavy items low and near the axle to keep a cart from tipping.

A removable or waterproof liner helps with rain and cleaning. The four cheapest models do not list one in the text we reviewed. Models such as the SereneLife state a removable liner at a higher tier. Without a liner, a plastic bag inside the basket protects groceries from rain.

faq.q: Will a folding wagon fit my trunk?
faq.a: The ROSONG states 22 x 9.8 x 7.5 inch folded. The Blomoba does not give a folded size in its listing. Measure your trunk before ordering a wagon. Fold the extendable handle down fully, since a protruding handle blocks a trunk lid.

faq.q: How can I make a budget cart last?
faq.a: Stay under the rating and let wet fabric dry before folding. Check the hinges and wheel mounts occasionally. Avoid dragging the cart over sharp edges. A dry wipe after use prevents mold on fabric wagons.
